I’ve been a client of Glendale Veterinary Clinic since Dr. Anne joined the practice many years ago. I followed her from another practice because I don’t know a better diagnostician than Dr. Anne.
In addition to her outstanding skills and expertise in diagnosing tricky conditions, she has performed several complex surgeries on my xl dogs and they have all been very successful and expertly done. No post op issues, ever. Always get follow up calls from her to check on her patients.

Update: Not sure what some people are ranting about. I’ve never been cheated or lied to by Dr. Anne. That’s absurd.

WARNING: DO NOT TRUST DR. ANNE!!
I normally don’t leave reviews, but I truly wish someone had warned me before I ever stepped foot in this clinic. My experience with Dr. Anne was one of the most unprofessional and frustrating experiences I’ve ever had. She comes across as confused, unsure, and lacking basic veterinary knowledge—and yet the clinic seems to know exactly how to rack up a bill.
I brought my dog in after noticing he was panting more than usual. Dr. Anne claimed she felt a lump and insisted on doing X-rays. Afterward, she told me he had fluid around his lungs, but then admitted she couldn’t read the X-rays properly—which made me wonder why they were even doing them in the first place. When I asked questions, she literally said, “I don’t know what this is.” Despite that, she said they’d need to drain the fluid and send it out for testing. Of course, we were charged for both the drainage attempt and for sending the X-rays to a “lab,” which I’m convinced is just some automated AI review.
She shaved my dog and attempted to drain the fluid but came back saying she couldn’t find a pocket and that we’d have to return the next day. Unfortunately, I made the mistake of trusting them and going back. The next day, we were suddenly told it wasn’t fluid at all—it was a mass, and that it was lymphoma. We were devastated and heartbroken. They prescribed prednisone to help shrink the mass, and we did everything they recommended, hoping it would help.
Soon after, my dog developed side effects: frequent urination, extreme thirst (which we expected to happen) but eventually, blood in his urine with a strong odor. I immediately called the clinic, and the receptionist—who was very kind and helpful—said we could get a general antibiotic but that they recommended a urine analysis to find the cause.
Two days later Dr. Anne called me herself, and she was rude, dismissive, and downright nasty. She basically accused me of lying about what her receptionist told me. I was shocked at how unprofessional and condescending she was, especially during such a difficult time for us.
I do want to point out that the receptionist and nurse were wonderful—they showed genuine care and compassion for my dog, unlike Dr. Anne, who acted like she was scared to even handle him. The only reason we returned the second time was because the receptionist assured us the owner of the clinic would take over. Somehow, we ended up stuck with Dr. Anne again, and it was another disaster.
We’ve since gone back to our old, trusted vet, and thank God for that. I genuinely feel sorry for the staff who have to work under Dr. Anne, and even more for the pets and pet parents who put their trust in her care.
Please save yourself the stress, heartache, and unnecessary charges—go somewhere else.

Worst experience at a vet.

We received a text asking if we could confirm or cancel our appointment made 2 days in advance. Unfortunately we weren’t able to confirm and couldn’t make it. My boyfriend called to reschedule, and was immediately told to put down a deposit for his next visit.

Completely reasonable but the sharp tone and being paywalled from knowing when we could reschedule to… that’s a no from me.

We decided to switch vets. He calls back and asks if his records could be transferred, the receptionist cuts in as his sentence is ending to say ‘we don’t do that, you can do it yourself’, sends us the records, clicked the phone on him without a bye.

two calls with Brianna, two counts of passive aggression. classic reception experience.

I missed my appointment on accident and when I called to reschedule, the receptionist was giving annoyed energy and immediately tells me I'll have to pay $80 deposit to reschedule. Doesn't ask me for my name, pets name, no other questions to even identify who I was. I wouldn't have minded paying the deposit since I've been coming here for a while and it was my mistake, but the bad vibes over the phone threw me off. Giving the energy of "ugh people are stupid and such an inconvenience". I cannot recommend this veterinary clinic enough. I moved to NY from MA/NH three years ago, where my cats always had excellent care, including one who, sadly, was diagnosed with large cell lymphoma. We had an incredible team back then who helped us give him the best care possible, but the disease was aggressive and we ultimately lost him.

Now, I’m looking after his brother, Louie, who continues to be by my side. I’ve always been extra cautious knowing his family history. The whole team here has been amazing - everyone from the front desk, who are always kind and helpful, to the doctors we’ve seen: Dr. Hess, Dr. Lindsey, and Dr. Anne. I feel so lucky to have them just 8 minutes away.

Louie was diagnosed with benign lymphoid hyperplasia two years ago, and now it looks like it may have progressed to IBD or small cell lymphoma. Even though that’s been scary to come to terms with, I’m so grateful for the care and attention we’ve had here. The vets and their team are truly the unsung heroes for those of us who love our pets like family. Thank you for all that you do for Louie and pets like him.
